rationale:
Split. The parent bundles five independent obligations.

Parts (a), (b) and (d) follow directly from SimonGMT's GeometricCurrentOn.affinePushforward with L = r⁻¹·id and b = −r⁻¹x:
- affinePullbackTestOn supplies the test forms;
- affinePushforward_apply gives Y ω = X(η^#ω);
- boundary_affinePushforward gives ∂Y = (∂X)_#;
- ContinuousAlternatingMap.map_smul_univ gives α∘(r⁻¹·id) = (rⁿ)⁻¹α.
These parts stay in the parent, whose implementation may import Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter06.AffineCurrentPushforward. That module is not in the import closure of the frozen Submission, so no child statement mentions it.

The remaining measure-theoretic content is split into five reusable lemmas:
- dilation_measure (Step 6): the Hⁿ scaling law. η is a measurable embedding and η_*(c·Hⁿ) = Hⁿ.
- weighted_tangent (Step 7(ii), orientation): weighted approximate tangent planes transfer under η.
- triple_image (Step 7(ii)): the image triple (η(M), θ∘η⁻¹, ξ∘η⁻¹) is a rectifiable triple. It depends on the previous two children.
- tau_action (Step 7(i)): the τ-action change of variables. Its left side is literally the expression used in the sibling ind_ae_blowup_limit.
- mass_bound (Step 5): M_W(Y) ≤ r^{−n}M_{η⁻¹W}(X) for any pair (X, Y) related by pull-back.

The parent derives (c) from triple_image, tau_action and θ′(η y) = θ(y) ∈ ℕ. It derives (e) from mass_bound applied to its own (a) and (b).

subproblems.title: Hⁿ scaling law for the dilation η_{x,r}: measurable embedding and measure preservation
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, x ∈ ℝ^P, r > 0 and η(y) := r⁻¹(y − x). Then η : ℝ^P → ℝ^P is a measurable embedding, and η is measure preserving from c·Hⁿ to Hⁿ, where Hⁿ = μHE[n] and c = ENNReal.ofReal((rⁿ)⁻¹); equivalently η_*(c·Hⁿ) = Hⁿ, i.e. Hⁿ(η⁻¹(B)) = rⁿ·Hⁿ(B) for every Borel B.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (x : Eucl P) (r : ℝ), 0 < r → MeasurableEmbedding (fun y : Eucl P => r⁻¹ • (y - x)) ∧ MeasurePreserving (fun y : Eucl P => r⁻¹ • (y - x)) (ENNReal.ofReal ((r ^ n)⁻¹) • (μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl P))) (μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl P))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Step 6 (change of variables) of the parent proof, isolated as a lemma. Conventions: ℝ^P := Eucl P (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin P)); Hⁿ := μHE[n]; η(y) := r⁻¹ • (y − x); c := ENNReal.ofReal((rⁿ)⁻¹).
1. η is a homeomorphism of ℝ^P. It is the composite e of the translation y ↦ y + (−x) (Homeomorph.addRight (−x)) and the dilation z ↦ r⁻¹ • z (Homeomorph.smulOfNeZero r⁻¹, valid because r⁻¹ ≠ 0). Indeed e(y) = r⁻¹ • (y + −x) = r⁻¹ • (y − x) = η(y) (sub_eq_add_neg), so ⇑e = η.
2. Measurable embedding. A homeomorphism between Borel spaces is a measurable embedding (Homeomorph.measurableEmbedding). By step 1, η is a measurable embedding; in particular it is measurable and injective. This is the first conjunct.
3. Preimages. For every B ⊆ ℝ^P, η⁻¹(B) = (z ↦ x + z) '' ((z ↦ r • z) '' B).
   (i) If η(y) ∈ B, put b := r⁻¹ • (y − x) ∈ B. Then x + r • b = x + r • r⁻¹ • (y − x) = x + (y − x) = y (smul_inv_smul₀ with r ≠ 0, add_sub_cancel).
   (ii) Conversely, η(x + r • b) = r⁻¹ • ((x + r • b) − x) = r⁻¹ • r • b = b ∈ B (add_sub_cancel_left, inv_smul_smul₀).
4. Scaling of Hⁿ, valid for every set B ⊆ ℝ^P.
   (i) Translation z ↦ x + z is an isometry (isometry_add_left x), so Hⁿ(x + S) = Hⁿ(S) for every S (Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image).
   (ii) (z ↦ r • z) '' B = r • B (Set.image_smul). Hence Hⁿ(r • B) = ‖r‖₊ⁿ • Hⁿ(B) (Measure.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_smul₀, since r ≠ 0).
   (iii) Combining (i), (ii) and step 3, Hⁿ(η⁻¹(B)) = ‖r‖₊ⁿ · Hⁿ(B).
5. Constant. In ℝ≥0∞, c · (‖r‖₊ⁿ : ℝ≥0∞) = 1. Since r > 0, ‖r‖ = r, so (‖r‖₊ⁿ : ℝ≥0∞) = ENNReal.ofReal(rⁿ) (ENNReal.ofReal_coe_nnreal, NNReal.coe_pow, coe_nnnorm, Real.norm_of_nonneg). As (rⁿ)⁻¹ ≥ 0, ENNReal.ofReal_mul gives c · ENNReal.ofReal(rⁿ) = ENNReal.ofReal((rⁿ)⁻¹ · rⁿ) = ENNReal.ofReal 1 = 1, because rⁿ ≠ 0 (inv_mul_cancel₀).
6. Measure preservation. η is measurable by step 2. For every measurable B, (η_*(c·Hⁿ))(B) = (c·Hⁿ)(η⁻¹(B)) = c · Hⁿ(η⁻¹(B)) (Measure.map_apply, Measure.smul_apply). By step 4(iii) this is c · ‖r‖₊ⁿ · Hⁿ(B), and by step 5 it equals Hⁿ(B). Two measures that agree on all measurable sets are equal (Measure.ext), so η_*(c·Hⁿ) = Hⁿ. Thus MeasurePreserving η (c·Hⁿ) Hⁿ, the second conjunct. ∎
proof_key_steps: η = (translation by −x) followed by (dilation by r⁻¹) is a homeomorphism, hence a measurable embedding (Homeomorph.measurableEmbedding).
Hⁿ(x + r·B) = ‖r‖₊ⁿHⁿ(B) by translation invariance (Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image) and Measure.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_smul₀.
ENNReal.ofReal((rⁿ)⁻¹)·‖r‖₊ⁿ = 1 for r > 0, so η_*(c·Hⁿ)(B) = Hⁿ(B) for measurable B; conclude by Measure.ext.

subproblems.title: Weighted approximate tangent spaces transfer under the dilation η_{x,r}
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, M ⊆ ℝ^P, θ : ℝ^P → ℝ, x, y ∈ ℝ^P, r > 0 and Q a linear subspace of ℝ^P. If Q is the weighted approximate tangent space of (M, θ) at y (HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M θ y Q), then Q is the weighted approximate tangent space at r⁻¹(y − x) of the image set {r⁻¹(w − x) : w ∈ M} with multiplicity z ↦ θ(x + r z).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (M : Set (Eucl P)) (θ : Eucl P → ℝ) (x y : Eucl P) (r : ℝ) (Q : Submodule ℝ (Eucl P)), 0 < r → HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M θ y Q → HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n ((fun w => r⁻¹ • (w - x)) '' M) (fun z => θ (x + r • z)) (r⁻¹ • (y - x)) Q
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: the 'Orientation' bullet of Step 7(ii) of the parent proof, isolated as a pointwise lemma. Conventions: ℝ^P := Eucl P (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin P)); Hⁿ := μHE[n]; η(w) := r⁻¹ • (w − x) (definitionally Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.blowUpMap x r); θ′(z) := θ(x + r • z).
Definition used (SimonGMT Chapter03.HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt): HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n N ϑ p Q means finrank ℝ Q = n and, for every f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P, ℝ), Tendsto (s ↦ ∫_{u ∈ blowUpMap p s '' N} f(u) · ϑ(p + s • u) dHⁿ(u)) (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 (ϑ(p) · ∫_{u ∈ Q} f(u) dHⁿ(u))), where blowUpMap p s (w) = s⁻¹ • (w − p).
Let z₀ := r⁻¹ • (y − x) = η(y). For f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P, ℝ) and t ∈ ℝ, write F_f(t) := ∫_{u ∈ blowUpMap y t '' M} f(u) · θ(y + t • u) dHⁿ(u). The hypothesis gives finrank Q = n and F_f → θ(y) · ∫_Q f dHⁿ along 𝓝[>] 0, for every f.
1. Value at the point: θ′(z₀) = θ(x + r • r⁻¹ • (y − x)) = θ(x + (y − x)) = θ(y), using r ≠ 0 (smul_inv_smul₀) and add_sub_cancel.
2. Dimension: finrank ℝ Q = n is part of the hypothesis and does not depend on the set or the multiplicity.
3. Set identity: for every s ∈ ℝ, blowUpMap z₀ s '' (η '' M) = blowUpMap y (r s) '' M. By Set.image_image the left side is the image of M under w ↦ s⁻¹ • (r⁻¹ • (w − x) − r⁻¹ • (y − x)). This equals s⁻¹ • r⁻¹ • ((w − x) − (y − x)) = (s⁻¹ r⁻¹) • (w − y) (smul_sub, smul_smul). Also (r s)⁻¹ = s⁻¹ r⁻¹ = r⁻¹ s⁻¹ (mul_inv_rev and commutativity; this holds in the field ℝ for every s, including s = 0). So the map is w ↦ (r s)⁻¹ • (w − y) = blowUpMap y (r s) w.
4. Weight identity: for all s, u, θ′(z₀ + s • u) = θ(x + r • (r⁻¹ • (y − x) + s • u)) = θ(x + (y − x) + (r s) • u) = θ(y + (r s) • u), by smul_add, smul_inv_smul₀ and smul_smul.
5. By steps 3 and 4, for every f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P, ℝ) and every s, ∫_{u ∈ blowUpMap z₀ s '' (η '' M)} f(u) · θ′(z₀ + s • u) dHⁿ(u) = F_f(r s). So the function whose limit is required equals F_f ∘ (s ↦ r s).
6. Tendsto (s ↦ r s) (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝[>] 0), via tendsto_nhdsWithin_iff:
   (i) s ↦ r s is continuous with value r · 0 = 0 at 0, so it tends to 𝓝 0 along 𝓝 0 and therefore along 𝓝[>] 0 ⊆ 𝓝 0 (nhdsWithin_le_nhds);
   (ii) for s > 0 we have r s > 0 (mul_pos), so the values eventually lie in (0, ∞) (eventually_nhdsWithin_of_forall).
7. Composing the hypothesis with step 6 (Tendsto.comp) gives F_f(r s) → θ(y) · ∫_Q f dHⁿ as s → 0⁺. By step 1 this limit is θ′(z₀) · ∫_Q f dHⁿ, and by step 5 this is exactly the required convergence for f.
8. Steps 2 and 7, the latter for every f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P, ℝ), give HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n (η '' M) θ′ (r⁻¹ • (y − x)) Q. ∎
proof_key_steps: θ′(η y) = θ(y) and finrank Q = n is unchanged.
blowUpMap (η y) s '' η(M) = blowUpMap y (r s) '' M and θ′(η y + s u) = θ(y + (r s) u), so the rescaled integral at s equals the original one at r s.
s ↦ r s maps 𝓝[>] 0 to 𝓝[>] 0; compose the defining limit with it (Tendsto.comp).

subproblems.title: The image of a rectifiable triple under the dilation η_{x,r} is a rectifiable triple
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, M ⊆ ℝ^P, θ : ℝ^P → ℝ, ξ : ℝ^P → Λ_n(ℝ^P) (NVector), x ∈ ℝ^P and r > 0. If (M, θ, ξ) is a rectifiable triple in ℝ^P (IsRectifiableTriple univ n M θ ξ), then so is (η(M), θ′, ξ′) with η(y) = r⁻¹(y − x), θ′(z) = θ(x + r z), ξ′(z) = ξ(x + r z).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (M : Set (Eucl P)) (θ : Eucl P → ℝ) (ξ : Eucl P → NVector (Eucl P) n) (x : Eucl P) (r : ℝ), 0 < r → IsRectifiableTriple (univ : Set (Eucl P)) n M θ ξ → IsRectifiableTriple (univ : Set (Eucl P)) n ((fun y => r⁻¹ • (y - x)) '' M) (fun z => θ (x + r • z)) (fun z => ξ (x + r • z))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Steps 6 and 7(ii) of the parent proof. Conventions. ℝ^P := Eucl P (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin P)); Hⁿ := μHE[n]; for x ∈ ℝ^P and r > 0, η(y) := r⁻¹ • (y − x) (definitionally Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.blowUpMap x r), θ′(z) := θ(x + r • z), ξ′(z) := ξ(x + r • z); c := ENNReal.ofReal((rⁿ)⁻¹).
0. Inversion identity (★0): x + r • η(y) = x + r • r⁻¹ • (y − x) = y for every y, since r ≠ 0 (smul_inv_smul₀, add_sub_cancel). Hence θ′ ∘ η = θ and ξ′ ∘ η = ξ. Also c = ENNReal.ofReal(·) ≠ ∞.
1. Sibling Submission.ind_rs_dilation_measurePreserving, applied to (P, n, x, r, r > 0), gives (a) η is a measurable embedding (in particular injective) and (b) MeasurePreserving η (c·Hⁿ) Hⁿ, i.e. η_*(c·Hⁿ) = Hⁿ.
2. Images of arbitrary sets: for every S ⊆ ℝ^P, Hⁿ(η(S)) = c · Hⁿ(S). Indeed Hⁿ(η(S)) = (η_*(c·Hⁿ))(η(S)) by 1(b). This equals (c·Hⁿ)(η⁻¹(η(S))) because MeasurableEmbedding.map_apply holds for every set. Since η⁻¹(η(S)) = S by injectivity (preimage_image_eq), the value is c · Hⁿ(S). In particular Hⁿ(S) = 0 implies Hⁿ(η(S)) = 0.
3. Restricted measures: Hⁿ⌞η(M) = η_*(c·(Hⁿ⌞M)). By MeasurePreserving.restrict_image_emb (from 1(a),(b)), η is measure preserving from (c·Hⁿ)⌞M to Hⁿ⌞η(M), and (c·Hⁿ)⌞M = c·(Hⁿ⌞M) (Measure.restrict_smul).
4. We verify the seven fields of IsRectifiableTriple univ n η(M) θ′ ξ′.
4a. subset: η(M) ⊆ univ trivially.
4b. nullMeasurableSet: let B := toMeasurable Hⁿ M. Then B is measurable and B =ᵐ[Hⁿ] M (NullMeasurableSet.toMeasurable_ae_eq, using the hypothesis that M is Hⁿ-null measurable). η(B) is measurable (MeasurableEmbedding.measurableSet_image). By ae_eq_set, Hⁿ(B \ M) = 0 and Hⁿ(M \ B) = 0. Injectivity gives η(B) \ η(M) = η(B \ M) and η(M) \ η(B) = η(M \ B) (Set.image_sdiff), and both are Hⁿ-null by step 2. So η(B) =ᵐ[Hⁿ] η(M), and η(M) is Hⁿ-null measurable (NullMeasurableSet.congr).
4c. countablyRectifiable: the hypothesis gives M₀ with Hⁿ(M₀) = 0 and maps F_j : ℝⁿ → ℝ^P with F_j LipschitzWith K_j and M ⊆ M₀ ∪ ⋃_j range F_j.
   - η is LipschitzWith ‖r⁻¹‖₊: dist(η a, η b) = ‖r⁻¹ • (a − x) − r⁻¹ • (b − x)‖ = ‖r⁻¹ • (a − b)‖ = ‖r⁻¹‖ · dist(a, b) (smul_sub, norm_smul, sub_sub_sub_cancel_right; LipschitzWith.of_dist_le_mul).
   - Take M₀′ := η(M₀), which is Hⁿ-null by step 2, and F′_j := η ∘ F_j, which is LipschitzWith (‖r⁻¹‖₊ · K_j) (LipschitzWith.comp).
   - Covering: if z = η(y) with y ∈ M, then either y ∈ M₀, so z ∈ η(M₀), or y = F_j(w) for some j, w, so z = F′_j(w) ∈ range F′_j. Hence η(M) ⊆ M₀′ ∪ ⋃_j range F′_j, which is CountablyRectifiable n η(M).
4d. pos: if z = η(y) with y ∈ M, then θ′(z) = θ(x + r • η(y)) = θ(y) > 0 by (★0) and the hypothesis.
4e. integrableOn: let K be compact (K ⊆ univ trivially).
   - η equals the homeomorphism (Homeomorph.addRight (−x)).trans (Homeomorph.smulOfNeZero r⁻¹ _), so η⁻¹(K) is compact (Homeomorph.isCompact_preimage).
   - The hypothesis therefore gives IntegrableOn θ (M ∩ η⁻¹(K)) Hⁿ.
   - η(M) ∩ K = η(M ∩ η⁻¹(K)) (Set.image_inter_preimage).
   - By MeasurePreserving.integrableOn_image (from 1(a),(b)), IntegrableOn θ′ (η(M ∩ η⁻¹(K))) Hⁿ ⇔ IntegrableOn (θ′ ∘ η) (M ∩ η⁻¹(K)) (c·Hⁿ). Here θ′ ∘ η = θ by (★0).
   - (c·Hⁿ)⌞S = c·(Hⁿ⌞S) (Measure.restrict_smul), and Integrable.smul_measure with c ≠ ∞ turns the hypothesis into integrability of θ for c·(Hⁿ⌞(M ∩ η⁻¹(K))). Hence IntegrableOn θ′ (η(M) ∩ K) Hⁿ.
4f. aestronglyMeasurable: by step 3 the measure is η_*(c·(Hⁿ⌞M)). By MeasurableEmbedding.aestronglyMeasurable_map_iff, ξ′ is AE-strongly measurable for it iff ξ′ ∘ η = ξ is AE-strongly measurable for c·(Hⁿ⌞M). This follows from the hypothesis AEStronglyMeasurable ξ (Hⁿ⌞M) by AEStronglyMeasurable.smul_measure.
4g. orients: by step 3 and MeasurableEmbedding.ae_map_iff, it suffices to show that, for (c·(Hⁿ⌞M))-a.e. y, the orientation property holds at the point η(y) for (η(M), θ′, ξ′).
   - The hypothesis gives the orientation property of (M, θ, ξ) at y for Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. y, and an a.e. property persists under scalar multiplication of the measure (Measure.ae_smul_measure).
   - Fix such a y with τ : Fin n → ℝ^P orthonormal, HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M θ y (span τ), and ξ(y) = simpleNVector τ or ξ(y) = −simpleNVector τ.
   - Sibling Submission.ind_rs_weightedTangent_dilation, applied to (P, n, M, θ, x, y, r, span τ, r > 0, that tangent hypothesis), gives HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n η(M) θ′ (r⁻¹ • (y − x)) (span τ), and r⁻¹ • (y − x) = η(y).
   - By (★0), ξ′(η(y)) = ξ(y) = ±simpleNVector τ.
   - So the same orthonormal τ witnesses the orientation property at η(y).
5. All fields hold, so IsRectifiableTriple univ n η(M) θ′ ξ′. ∎
proof_key_steps: x + r·η(y) = y, so θ′∘η = θ and ξ′∘η = ξ; η is a measurable embedding with η_*(c·Hⁿ) = Hⁿ (sibling ind_rs_dilation_measurePreserving).
Hⁿ(η(S)) = c·Hⁿ(S) for all S and Hⁿ⌞η(M) = η_*(c·Hⁿ⌞M) (MeasurePreserving.restrict_image_emb).
Null-measurability via η(toMeasurable M) =ᵐ η(M); countable rectifiability via η(M₀) and the Lipschitz maps η∘F_j.
Positivity by θ′∘η = θ; local integrability via η(M)∩K = η(M∩η⁻¹K), η⁻¹K compact, and MeasurePreserving.integrableOn_image.

AE-strong measurability and the a.e. orientation property via MeasurableEmbedding.aestronglyMeasurable_map_iff / ae_map_iff, with the tangent transfer from sibling ind_rs_weightedTangent_dilation and ξ′(η y) = ξ(y).

subproblems.title: Change of variables for the τ-action under the dilation η_{x,r}
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, M ⊆ ℝ^P, θ : ℝ^P → ℝ, ξ : ℝ^P → NVector, x ∈ ℝ^P, r > 0 and ω an n-form on ℝ^P. Then tauAction n M θ ξ (y ↦ (rⁿ)⁻¹ ω(r⁻¹(y − x))) = tauAction n η(M) θ′ ξ′ ω, where η(y) = r⁻¹(y − x), θ′(z) = θ(x + r z), ξ′(z) = ξ(x + r z).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (M : Set (Eucl P)) (θ : Eucl P → ℝ) (ξ : Eucl P → NVector (Eucl P) n) (x : Eucl P) (r : ℝ) (ω : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) n), 0 < r → tauAction n M θ ξ (fun y => (r ^ n)⁻¹ • ω (r⁻¹ • (y - x))) = tauAction n ((fun y => r⁻¹ • (y - x)) '' M) (fun z => θ (x + r • z)) (fun z => ξ (x + r • z)) ω
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Step 7(i) (Formula) of the parent proof, with the change of variables (★) of Step 6. Conventions: ℝ^P := Eucl P (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin P)); Hⁿ := μHE[n]; η(y) := r⁻¹ • (y − x) (definitionally Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.blowUpMap x r); θ′(z) := θ(x + r • z); ξ′(z) := ξ(x + r • z).
Definition used: tauAction n S ϑ ζ ω = ∫_{y ∈ S} ϑ(y) · ζ(y)(ω(y)) dHⁿ(y), a Bochner set integral, which is 0 when the integrand is not integrable. No integrability is assumed or needed below.
1. Left side. ξ(y) ∈ NVector (ℝ^P) n is a continuous ℝ-linear map on covectors (Covector →L[ℝ] ℝ), so ξ(y)((rⁿ)⁻¹ • ω(η y)) = (rⁿ)⁻¹ · ξ(y)(ω(η y)) (map_smul, smul_eq_mul). Hence the integrand of the left side is θ(y) · ((rⁿ)⁻¹ · ξ(y)(ω(η y))) = (rⁿ)⁻¹ · (θ(y) · ξ(y)(ω(η y))). By integral_const_mul (valid without integrability), LHS = (rⁿ)⁻¹ · ∫_{y ∈ M} θ(y) · ξ(y)(ω(η y)) dHⁿ.
2. Right side, change of variables. Let g(z) := θ(x + r • z) · ξ(x + r • z)(ω(z)). Then RHS = ∫_{z ∈ η(M)} g(z) dHⁿ(z). The function η equals Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.blowUpMap x r definitionally (blowUpMap x r y = r⁻¹ • (y − x)). The accepted declaration Submission.lpf_wtc_blowup_setIntegral_image, applied with Q := P, n, y := x, r, S := M, g and 0 < r, gives ∫_{z ∈ blowUpMap x r '' M} g(z) dHⁿ = (rⁿ)⁻¹ · ∫_{y ∈ M} g(blowUpMap x r y) dHⁿ. So RHS = (rⁿ)⁻¹ · ∫_{y ∈ M} g(η(y)) dHⁿ(y).
2′. Self-contained derivation of the identity used in step 2 (use it only if Submission.lpf_wtc_blowup_setIntegral_image is unavailable in the working tree; it needs no sibling lemma). Let c := ENNReal.ofReal((rⁿ)⁻¹).
   (i) η is the homeomorphism (Homeomorph.addRight (−x)).trans (Homeomorph.smulOfNeZero r⁻¹ _) (sub_eq_add_neg), so it is a measurable embedding (Homeomorph.measurableEmbedding).
   (ii) For every B ⊆ ℝ^P, η⁻¹(B) = (z ↦ x + z) '' ((z ↦ r • z) '' B): if η(y) ∈ B then y = x + r • (r⁻¹ • (y − x)); conversely η(x + r • b) = b. Hence Hⁿ(η⁻¹(B)) = Hⁿ(r • B) = ‖r‖₊ⁿ · Hⁿ(B) (Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image with isometry_add_left x; Set.image_smul; Measure.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_smul₀, r ≠ 0).
   (iii) c · ‖r‖₊ⁿ = ENNReal.ofReal((rⁿ)⁻¹ · rⁿ) = 1 (ENNReal.ofReal_mul, Real.norm_of_nonneg, inv_mul_cancel₀). With Measure.map_apply and Measure.ext, (ii) gives η_*(c·Hⁿ) = Hⁿ, i.e. MeasurePreserving η (c·Hⁿ) Hⁿ.
   (iv) MeasurePreserving.setIntegral_image_emb (from (i), (iii)) gives ∫_{η(M)} g dHⁿ = ∫_M g ∘ η d(c·Hⁿ). Then (c·Hⁿ)⌞M = c·(Hⁿ⌞M) (Measure.restrict_smul) and integral_smul_measure give ∫_M g ∘ η d(c·Hⁿ) = c.toReal · ∫_M g ∘ η dHⁿ. Finally c.toReal = (rⁿ)⁻¹ (ENNReal.toReal_ofReal, as (rⁿ)⁻¹ ≥ 0). This is the identity of step 2.
3. Pointwise identity. x + r • η(y) = x + r • r⁻¹ • (y − x) = y (smul_inv_smul₀ with r ≠ 0, add_sub_cancel), so g(η(y)) = θ(y) · ξ(y)(ω(η y)) for every y.
4. By steps 2 and 3, RHS = (rⁿ)⁻¹ · ∫_{y ∈ M} θ(y) · ξ(y)(ω(η y)) dHⁿ, which equals the LHS by step 1. ∎
proof_key_steps: Linearity of ξ(y) pulls (rⁿ)⁻¹ out of the left integral (map_smul, integral_const_mul).
The accepted Submission.lpf_wtc_blowup_setIntegral_image with g(z) = θ(x+rz)ξ(x+rz)(ω z) rewrites the right integral as (rⁿ)⁻¹∫_M g(η y) dHⁿ.
g(η y) = θ(y)ξ(y)(ω(η y)) because x + r·η(y) = y.

subproblems.title: Mass bound for a current defined by pull-back along the dilation η_{x,r}
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, X, Y ∈ D_n(ℝ^P), x ∈ ℝ^P and r > 0. Assume (A) for every ω ∈ D^n(ℝ^P) there is η ∈ D^n(ℝ^P) with η(y) = (rⁿ)⁻¹ω(r⁻¹(y − x)) for all y, and (B) Y(ω) = X(η) whenever η(y) = (rⁿ)⁻¹ω(r⁻¹(y − x)) for all y. Then M_W(Y) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal((rⁿ)⁻¹)·M_{{y : r⁻¹(y−x) ∈ W}}(X) for every W ⊆ ℝ^P.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (X Y : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Eucl P)) n) (x : Eucl P) (r : ℝ), 0 < r → (∀ ω : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Eucl P)) n, ∃ η : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Eucl P)) n, ∀ y, (η : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) n) y = (r ^ n)⁻¹ • (ω : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) n) (r⁻¹ • (y - x))) → (∀ ω η : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Eucl P)) n, (∀ y, (η : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) n) y = (r ^ n)⁻¹ • (ω : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) n) (r⁻¹ • (y - x))) → Y ω = X η) → ∀ W : Set (Eucl P), Y.massOn W ≤ ENNReal.ofReal ((r ^ n)⁻¹) * X.massOn {y | r⁻¹ • (y - x) ∈ W}
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Step 5 (part (e), the mass bound) of the parent proof, stated for any pair (X, Y) related by pull-back along η. Conventions: ℝ^P := Eucl P; φ(y) := r⁻¹ • (y − x); V := {y : φ(y) ∈ W} = φ⁻¹(W).
Definitions used (SimonGMT Chapter06.Mass):
- T.massOn W = sSup {ENNReal.ofReal(T ω) : ω ∈ massAdmissibleOn univ n W};
- ω ∈ massAdmissibleOn univ n W iff tsupport ω ⊆ W and covectorEuclideanNorm(ω(z)) ≤ 1 for all z.
1. Reduction. By sSup_le, it suffices to show ENNReal.ofReal(Y ω) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal((rⁿ)⁻¹) · X.massOn V for every ω ∈ massAdmissibleOn univ n W. Fix such ω.
2. Choose η by (A): η ∈ TestFormOn univ n with η(y) = (rⁿ)⁻¹ • ω(φ(y)) for all y. Let η̂ := rⁿ • η; it lies in TestFormOn univ n, a submodule. For every y, η̂(y) = rⁿ • (rⁿ)⁻¹ • ω(φ(y)) = ω(φ(y)), because rⁿ ≠ 0 (smul_smul, mul_inv_cancel₀). So η̂ = ω ∘ φ as functions.
3. η̂ is admissible for X.massOn V.
   (i) covectorEuclideanNorm(η̂(y)) = covectorEuclideanNorm(ω(φ(y))) ≤ 1 for all y, by admissibility of ω.
   (ii) φ is continuous, so tsupport(ω ∘ φ) ⊆ φ⁻¹(tsupport ω) (tsupport_comp_subset_preimage). Since tsupport ω ⊆ W, this is contained in φ⁻¹(W) = V (preimage_mono).
   Hence ENNReal.ofReal(X η̂) ≤ X.massOn V (GeometricCurrentOn.le_massOn).
4. Value of Y. As test forms, η = (rⁿ)⁻¹ • η̂, since (rⁿ)⁻¹ • rⁿ • η = η (smul_smul, inv_mul_cancel₀). By (B) applied to the pair (ω, η), Y ω = X η. By linearity of X (X.toCurrent is ℝ-linear, map_smul), Y ω = (rⁿ)⁻¹ · X η̂.
5. Since (rⁿ)⁻¹ ≥ 0, ENNReal.ofReal((rⁿ)⁻¹ · X η̂) = ENNReal.ofReal((rⁿ)⁻¹) · ENNReal.ofReal(X η̂) (ENNReal.ofReal_mul). This holds whatever the sign of X η̂.
6. By steps 3 and 5 and monotonicity of multiplication in ℝ≥0∞, ENNReal.ofReal(Y ω) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal((rⁿ)⁻¹) · X.massOn V.
7. Step 6 holds for every admissible ω, so step 1 gives Y.massOn W ≤ ENNReal.ofReal((rⁿ)⁻¹) · X.massOn {y | r⁻¹ • (y − x) ∈ W}. ∎
proof_key_steps: For admissible ω, take η from (A) and η̂ := rⁿη; then η̂ = ω∘φ, so |η̂(y)| ≤ 1 and tsupport η̂ ⊆ φ⁻¹(W).
Y ω = X η = (rⁿ)⁻¹X η̂ by (B) and linearity; ENNReal.ofReal_mul and sSup_le give the bound.
